title: Marriage
lead: From Genesis 2 ("they become one flesh") to the wedding of the Lamb in Revelation 19, the Bible pictures marriage, especially of a man and a woman, as a bond some texts call a covenant (Malachi 2:14), and as an image of God's love for his people. It also records polygamous and broken marriages.

sections.b: Genesis 2:18–25 sets the pattern most later texts refer back to: a partner who is the man's match, leaving father and mother, clinging, and one flesh. The Law regulates marriage and divorce (Deuteronomy 24:1–4); Proverbs praises a good wife (Proverbs 31:10–31); the Song of Songs celebrates love. The prophets picture God as Israel's husband (Hosea 2:16–20; Isaiah 54:5; Jeremiah 2:2), and Malachi says God hates divorce, calling a wife "your partner by covenant" (Malachi 2:14–16). Jesus quotes Genesis 1:27 and 2:24 against easy divorce (Matthew 19:3–9). Paul uses Genesis 2:24 for sexual ethics and for Christ and the church (1 Corinthians 6:16; Ephesians 5:31–32). The Bible's stories also show polygamy and broken marriages without approving them.
sections.refs: Genesis 2:18–25; Deuteronomy 24:1–4; Hosea 2:16–20; Malachi 2:14–16; Matthew 19:3–9; 1 Corinthians 6:16; Ephesians 5:22–33; Revelation 19:7–9
